checked_claims.claim: For g>=2, W_k H^k(M_{g,n})/(Phi_{g,n}^k+Psi_{g,n}^k) is isomorphic to the direct sum over |lambda|=n of W_k H^{k-n}(M_g;V_lambda) tensor V_{lambda^T}.
checked_claims.note: This is SRC-0002 Lemma 3.1(a), quoted from corpus/text/SRC-0002.txt. Phi is the sum of forgetful pullbacks of W_k H^k(M_{g,n-1}); Psi is generated by psi_i times Phi^{k-2}. The proof uses the smooth proper n-fold universal curve C^n -> M_g, Deligne degeneration of Leray, Kunneth with i_s in {0,1,2}, and symplectic contractions of (R^1 pi_* Q)^{tensor n} from pairwise diagonals, citing Petersen-Tavakol-Yin. The attempt's independent sketch (psi generating R^2 because it restricts to the canonical class) is coarser than the paper's projector pi_2, but the load-bearing input is the published lemma, which is listed as SRC-0002. The isomorphism is applied to the pure weight-k quotient, so vanishing of the underlying Q-vector spaces on the right kills the quotient as a Hodge structure.

Lemma 3.1 at (g,n,k)=(6,6,26) places every summand in W_26 H^{20}(M_6;V_lambda) with |lambda|=6. V_lambda is a finite-dimensional rational symplectic local system, hence a Q Mod_6-module. Harer vcd(Mod_6)=4g-5=19; M_6 is an orbifold K(pi,1), so H^{20}(M_6;V_lambda)=H^{20}(Mod_6;V_lambda). A torsion-free finite-index subgroup Gamma has cd=19, so H^{20}(Gamma;V_lambda)=0; the core is normal of finite index and the same cd. Hochschild-Serre for the finite quotient with Q-coefficients has vanishing positive-degree rows, hence H^{20}(Mod_6;V_lambda)=0. W_26 of the zero group is zero. This is strictly above vcd, not the blocked equality 26=vcd(M_{6,6}).

Phi is the sum of pullbacks of W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,5}). For n=5>=1, vcd(PMod_{6,5})=vcd(Mod_{6,5})=4g-4+n=25. Degree 26 exceeds this bound, so H^{26}(M_{6,5};Q)=0 as stack/group cohomology with rational coefficients (FND-0036). Pullbacks of zero vanish. Finite-index Hochschild-Serre is unnecessary here but valid.

checked_claims.claim: W_24 H^{24}(M_{6,5};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-12).
checked_claims.note: THM-0005 gives CKgP and tautological Chow for n<=c(g) with c(6)=5, so it applies on the nose to M_{6,5}. SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3: CKgP implies the cycle class map surjects onto every W_k H^k, hence even-degree lowest-weight groups are pure Hodge-Tate. Proposition 4.5 strengthens this to W_k H^k(M_{6,5})=RH^k(M_{6,5}) for every k, in particular k=24. Algebraic classes in degree 24 have type (12,12)=Q(-12). Polarizable pure weight-24 Hodge structures are semisimple, so the group is a finite direct sum of Q(-12). No upgrade from mere Tate type to algebraicity is assumed: CKgP supplies algebraicity first.

checked_claims.claim: Psi_{6,6}^{26}, and hence W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q), is a finite direct sum of Q(-13).
checked_claims.note: From CLM-0135-2 and CLM-0135-3, W_26 H^{26}=Phi+Psi=Psi as subspaces of a pure polarizable weight-26 structure. Psi is generated by cup products of psi_i (algebraic, type Q(-1)) with pullbacks of W_24 H^{24}(M_{6,5}) (type Q(-12)). Pullback along the smooth forgetful maps is type (0,0). The image is therefore a quotient of a finite sum of Q(-13). FND-0033: polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of fixed weight are semisimple, so a quotient of a Tate sum is a Tate sum of the same type. Equivalently, tautological rings are closed under psi and forgetful pullback, so Psi subset RH^{26} and is algebraic of type Q(-13). Finite rank is automatic for finite-type stacks.

checked_claims.claim: W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8).
checked_claims.note: FND-0001: for d=3g-3+n=21, Poincare duality of the smooth finite-type DM stack identifies W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16} with W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21). Tate twist: Q(-13)(21)=Q(8). The case r=0 is included; the theorem's disproof clause requires a surviving non-Tate summand, which the argument excludes. Coefficients are Q throughout; no integral-coefficient or coarse-space comparison is used.

checked_claims.claim: Kunneth/Leray indexing of the remaining all-R^1 term is H^{k-n}(M_g;(R^1)^{tensor n}) with lowest weight k, matching W_k on both sides of Lemma 3.1.
checked_claims.note: Each i_s in {0,1,2} and p+sum i_s=k. After removing some i_s=0 (Phi) and some i_s=2 (Psi), one has i_1=...=i_n=1, so p=k-n. R^1 pi_* Q is the pure weight-1 symplectic local system of the closed universal curve, not the mixed R^1 of the n-punctured forgetful map (FND-0020/FND-0037). V_lambda has weight |lambda|=n, so H^{k-n}(M_g;V_lambda) has weights >=k and W_k is its lowest-weight piece. The argument never labels that piece as W_{k-n}.

checked_claims.claim: All identifications are stack-level rational Betti/MHS statements for M_{g,n}, not coarse spaces or integral coefficients.
checked_claims.note: The attempt sets X_{g,n}=M_{g,n} as the smooth DM stack. Group cohomology of PMod/Mod with Q-coefficients computes stack cohomology. Finite group cohomology with Q-coefficients vanishes in positive degrees, which is used in Hochschild-Serre and in S_n-multiplicity spaces V_{lambda^T} (those are rational Specht modules, not a source of non-Tate Hodge types). No graph-automorphism invariants/coinvariants appear.

checked_claims.claim: Omitting Casnati-Ekedahl support and stable-graph strata does not leave an unaccounted summand in the exact group.
checked_claims.note: Lemma 3.1 plus the two vcd vanishings plus CKgP at n=5 compute the whole group W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q), not a support subquotient. Complementary compactification or CE terms are not an omitted hypothesis of this argument.

finding_candidates.statement: SRC-0002 Lemma 3.1 at (g,n,k)=(6,6,26) identifies the primitive quotient of W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) with a sum of W_26 H^{20}(M_6;V_lambda) over |lambda|=6. Harer vcd(Mod_6)=4g-5=19 is strictly less than 20 and applies to every finite-dimensional rational Mod_6-module, so every such summand vanishes as a Q-vector space and as a mixed Hodge structure. This is not vanishing at the target degree 26=vcd(M_{6,6}).

proof_dependency_checks.note: Poincare duality W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) with d=21 is used exactly as recorded; twist arithmetic Q(-13)(21)=Q(8) matches the target dictionary.

Semisimplicity of the pure polarizable weight-26 (equivalently weight -16) corner is used to pass from a Tate quotient/subobject to an actual Hodge-structure isomorphism. No exotic extension gap remains.
Used only as a constraint: vanishing is never inferred from 26=vcd(M_{6,6}). Auxiliary applications are at degree 20>19 on M_6 with local coefficients and at degree 26>25 on M_{6,5}.
Load-bearing for Phi_{6,6}^{26}=0: H^{26}(M_{6,5};Q)=0 because 26>vcd=25. The attempt does not rerun the mixed-R^1 forgetful Leray of FND-0037.
c(6)=5, so M_{6,5} has CKgP and tautological Chow. Combined with SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3/Proposition 4.5 this makes W_24 H^{24}(M_{6,5}) algebraic of type Q(-12).
Lemma 3.1(a) is the primitive-quotient formula; Lemma 4.3 and Proposition 4.5 and Table 1 supply algebraicity of pure-weight groups in the CKgP range, including (g,n)=(6,5).
Listed source behind THM-0005 CKgP ranges (Theorem 1.4). Not quoted independently in the argument; load-bearing only through THM-0005.

strongest_attack: Strongest attack: the primitive slot W_26 H^{20}(M_6;V_lambda) might survive because (i) Harer vcd(Mod_6)=19 could fail for nontrivial symplectic local systems, (ii) Lemma 3.1's W_k H^{k-n} notation might be a weight-shifted group that is not a subspace of ordinary H^{20}, or (iii) the attempt's psi-versus-R^2 sketch might not match Petersen's projector, so Phi+Psi might not exhaust the non-primitive Kunneth summands. Outcome: all three fail. (i) Virtual cohomological dimension is the cohomological dimension of a torsion-free finite-index subgroup and therefore annihilates H^{>19} with every finite-dimensional rational coefficient module; the stack M_6 is an orbifold K(Mod_6,1), and Hochschild-Serre for a finite quotient has vanishing positive-degree rational cohomology. (ii) If the underlying Q-vector space H^{20}(M_6;V_lambda) is zero then every weight piece, including W_26, is zero; separately, V_lambda has weight |lambda|=6 so ordinary H^{20} already has weights >=26, matching the W_26 index. (iii) The load-bearing identification is the published SRC-0002 Lemma 3.1, not the informal projector sketch. Secondary attacks also fail: Poincare duality and the twist Q(-13)(21)=Q(8) match FND-0001; FND-0033 kills any semisimplification gap; CKgP gives algebraicity of W_24 H^{24}(M_{6,5}) rather than upgrading mere Tate type; the closed-curve R^1 is pure of weight 1, so FND-0020/FND-0037 mixed punctured-curve coefficients are not used; omitted CE/stable-pair geometry is not a missing summand once the whole exact group is identified.
theorem_statement: The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.
